quests.briefing: Bram Ostrowski sells you a waxed sheet of the estuary. A road is drawn where summer water should be. He will not say who walked it. He will take calories or a favour-by-mass. The sheet smells of lamp oil and fish glue.

stages.text: Bought / copied item_map_sheet_ice_road. The wax takes a fingerprint and keeps it. Channel markers on the sheet do not match the last Sector 4 lamp you know.
Compared to Kittiwake log (if owned). The launch's hand is eleven days past the Exchange. Ostrowski's hand is this year. The road exists on only one of them. The ice has not been asked.
Asked a Lamplighter about Kilometre 19. Ivy confirms the post. She does not confirm the road. She does not cross.
Survived the asking. No exception was requested. The ledger still shows 19 lit. You have a fragment and a direction that is only a direction in winter.

choices.text: He wraps the sheet in the same paper he uses for maps that exist in all seasons. He does not wish you luck. He wishes you a freeze.
Your copy smears at Kilometre 19. His does not. He notices. He does not raise the price. He files you as a person who copies.
He puts the sheet away. The estuary remains a rumour with a smell. Ivy will still light 19. Yara will still open a road you cannot prove.

quests.briefing: A man stands off the weighbridge plate so he will not be charged as cargo. Census Clerk Grade III Edor Vale. A return in triplicate. Three of your people are already written, occupations wrong by one each. He offers to read it twice. The Tollman charges for the introduction.

stages.text: Heard the form. Heading, occupancy, reconstruction pool, ice window. He did not skip a field. You may ask him to start again.
Confirmed or denied three occupations. Adjacent errors. Mason / caretaker. Clerk / clerk-grade. Vet assistant / vet. He corrects in the same hand. He thanks you for the truth without using the word.
Hatch wait: allowed or refused. If allowed, he keeps off the step with a stove-tin. If refused, he goes as far as the boom.
Sela's card (optional). He copies the number. He does not take the laminate. UNCONFIRMED until someone who can confirm, confirms.

choices.text: He sleeps in the ash with the tin. Survivors who cannot sleep will knock the tin, not the hatch. In the morning the pink copy has dew in the folds.
He goes. He does not call it a refusal. Ormund will. The weighbridge keeps his stool for him.
He writes the number as if it were a date of birth: once, slowly. He does not look at Sela as a line item while she is in the room. He looks after.

quests.briefing: Yara Holm at the Gate. The boom is up for a freeze that has a length. Fourteen days this window. Outfit three: warmth, iodine, food, welders' glass. Lit hours on the board. Dark ice is not a metaphor.

stages.text: Column kitted. Glass on faces. Iodine in a tin that will freeze shut if you leave it in a pocket. The axle ledger takes your mass.
Waystation A reached. Four bunks. Filter notches. Stove regulator in place. Home still ticking.
Dark ice not walked (or walked). If you waited: she marks you rare. If you did not: remarks column, and she does not fetch.
Returned or wintered A4. The last bunk is wettest. The window does not care which you chose. The ice will.

choices.text: Hours and cold. The beacon stays honest. Yara does not thank you. She puts you on the overnight.
The ice is thick. Thick is not lit. An accident is written whether or not you are in it.
You spend the closed window on A4. Filter at eleven. Do not file a twelfth notch. Home degrades without you.

quests.briefing: The desalination plant is not abandoned. It is staffed, failing, named. Leva Quist's minutes are current. Steam visible toward a place with numbers. Resin is a gift or an insult depending on how you set it down.

stages.text: Grade Hut entered. Volume 12 open. Motion: that we keep running. Carried. A failed valve-seat for a paperweight.
Membrane Hall toured. Fume at chest height. Tuesday's difference on the drum rims. The dipper stays on the nail unless you steal it.
Resin: delivered or refused. Delivered: she counts aloud. Refused: she counts anyway. The count is short.
Steam line seen. Canal wheel painted red-white-red. Cluster on the far end of a pipe. Not a rumour.

choices.text: She does not say thank you. She marks a drum. Salt trade opens like a valve, which is to say: slowly, with a gauge.
She needed it anyway. You are a visitor who watched. Watching is not a shift.
That was your word. Ours is Municipal Desalination 8. The stop order didn't come. We didn't stop.

quests.briefing: Cluster Gatehouse. Cream paint. A keypad under plastic. They will ask for an Allocation number. Twelve is a known discrepancy. They have a procedure. Guest housing is Block C. The Quad has chains and no seats.

stages.text: Number stated, or none. Twelve opens a file. None opens a different tab of the same binder. Both are procedures.
Block C accepted, or Gatehouse floor. Metal plates versus paper tags versus tiles. Steam or no steam.
Quad walked. Four cultivars, two yellow. Missing-persons strip of Sector 4 trades. One of them is yours.
Playground brass: left or taken. Silent. The chain hangs. The Office notes mass if mass leaves.

choices.text: The bell does not ring. A clerk says known discrepancy as if it were a weather. Badge: GUEST / BLOCK C or UNSCHEDULED. Both print on paper.
They do not invent a number for you. The floor of the gatehouse has a blanket that has been washed. The thermometer still reads like survival.
No alarm. No speech. Later, a mass note. The chain does not swing. You have brass in the pack.
Children pass. Adults file you. The yellow leaves tick against the trough.

quests.briefing: Ormund's right-hand drawer. The Sector 4 Schedule, complete. Names you know. Names you buried. He turns pages with two fingers. He does not ask how you feel about a column.

stages.text: Read Sole. SOLE, MARGIT J. Records Clerk II. RUR 9. Score 41.2. NOT ALLOCATED. He does not offer to fix her.
Read Renn. RENN, HALVARD — water engineer — allocated — NOT ARRIVED — 12-B UNCONFIRMED. A dependent line that may be Sela if she is yours to name.
Searched Frayne. Absent. RUR 11 does not produce an allocation. He will not write her in because you asked.
Asked about 12-C (optional). He has a string-tied folder. He may show it. He may say it is for a later hour.

choices.text: He does. Completeness is not execution. He executes. He does not raise his voice at her number.
He does. If Sela is present he does not look at her until the line is finished. Then he does.
The Schedule is not a petition. He offers no further sentence.
That is a different folder. You may see it after you have slept in a numbered building. Occupancy first.

quests.briefing: Three names. Thirty days. Occupations as scored or as observed. The ice will not wait for a better feeling. Kit for salt and UV if they go. Tell the people who stay. The duty roster will have holes.

stages.text: Named survivors reviewed. Wrong-by-one occupations corrected or left. Faces. Tools. Who still has skin that will hate brine.
Honour / substitute / refuse. Flags. No combat. The next paragraph of the form.
If sending: kitted. Glass, iodine, salve, calories. Axle ledger. Yara's lit hours.
Remaining shelter informed. Morale as a quiet room, not a speech. A blank on the roster where a name was.

choices.text: You send the three as written. Calories and medicine will come north-to-south on a rate the Office calls regular. The three take Ice Road fatigue and salt-rash risk. Cluster trust ticks up. The people who remain eat easier and sleep worse. One of the three may refuse to return. That refusal will also be filed.

You send three other people. Ormund notes irregular. Yara respects that the ice got three who would walk lit. Edor does not: the names are wrong, and names are his job. Later, an audit. Possibly a second levy. The roster at home still has holes, just different holes.

You refuse in writing, or by not writing. No shots. Edor waits in the ash. Ice Road access withdraws after eleven days if the Office asks the Cutters to treat you as dark. Ormund does not say or else. The next form is 12-C. Threatening prose unlocks on Office scenes. The three named people hear that they were named.

quests.briefing: Bank two trips. Cluster steam clock starts. Leva has the forty-eight hour math in her mouth without making it a threat. Resin, brass, iodine, two workers, an outfall shift. Sector 4's thirst and District 8's thirst are one job until they are not.

stages.text: Diagnosed. Gauge, difference, canal wheel, substation thermometer. Not ideology. Valves.
Gathered. Resin drums, brass seats, iodine, two bodies who will stand the apron.
Outfall shift. Health, salt, the clipboard that is ceremonial until you make it not.
Strip / local salvage / let drop. The indoors will feel it or the Verge will, or both, or neither in time.

choices.text: You strip what Sector 4 can spare: Rebuilders brass, iodine, filters. The bank holds. Cluster lives. Allotments thirst clock shortens. Frayne's minutes record a shortage without naming you. Medical market shock. The playground chains do not get their seats back. The tin behind your filter, if you raided it, is lighter. Nobody mentions it.
Spent stack, recoating jig, Salt's hidden iodine key. Yield low. Integrity to forty percent if the apron is stood. Nobody in the Verge goes thirstier today. Tomorrow's Tuesday is still short.

You let steam die. 211 people who have not practised this cold. Office legitimacy cracks. Salt may offer a separate bargain — plant over paper. Unifier path hardens because a treaty wants a room that can still hold heat. Children take coats. Attendance is still taken.

quests.briefing: Reconstruction Order 12-C: unlisted occupants of authenticated Allocation 12 are a labour reserve. Published. Nobody in Sector 4 had a copy that survived. Ormund has one. He will come south when the ice allows. You may carry a copy to Sole. She will file it. She will not sign it. Voss will want the pool.

stages.text: Copy obtained. item_order_12c. String tie. Civil-service present tense. No please. No or else.
Sole (optional). Drown boat. She files. She does not sign. Completeness versus execution, same noun, opposite people.
Voss (optional). He wants the pool. He will call it conscription and mean it as a compliment to himself. Intercept risk on a levy column.
Hatch prepared. Roster. Temperature. Whether anyone writes a name. Whether the outer dog is thrown.

choices.text: She reads it twice, which is not Edor's habit, it is hers. She blots the date. She does not blot the refusal.
He wants names. He will not pay the Office's rate. He will pay in patrols at the Gate. The Cutters will not like the patrols.
The paper lives in your pack like a spare filter. It does not clean anything. It is still a paper that moves people.
Forty days quiet. A receipt in the ash, cousin to a card in a freezer bag. Different district. Same temperature.

quests.briefing: Forms at the outer hatch. Escort in faded Continuity jackets. Temperature. The game stops talking. This is not Sela's arrival, or it is Sela's arrival and this. Open or keep shut. Authenticate, house, or levy. Or wait forty days. Write on the duty roster, or do not.

stages.text: Open or shut. The dog on the hatch is a fact. So is the quiet.
If open: authenticate / house / levy. Numbers, Block C tags, three names. Edor asks to speak first if he is there.
If shut: forty days. No combat. The escort remains on a rota you cannot see. Then a receipt.
Roster. A name in a Cluster hand, a name in yours, or a blank that is also a decision.

choices.text: Some of yours live numbered in Block C. The bunker is easier to feed. The roster has names that did not sleep there last winter.
Columns both ways. Receipts in triplicate. Nobody is shot. Sela claimed as dependent if present and if she heard it.
District 8 continues. Forty empty apartments stay empty. Edor's return may be found later, incomplete, in a good hand.
Ink on a chart that was always blank. The people who see it in the morning will know which sentence you believed.
The chart stays honest about who this hole was built for. It stays dishonest about who kept it.

quests.briefing: A five-sledge salt convoy from the coast is stalled at Kilometre 14 with cracked runners. The frost is deepening, but the tide is due to turn in twenty-four hours. Deliver hardwood runner braces and escort the cargo before the ice begins to flex.

stages.text: Carry runner hardwood and tallow grease to the stalled sledges at Kilometre 14.
Jack the heavy salt sledge and screw new steel-shod runners onto the split ash frame.
Escort the column through the slush seam while the ice is still quiet.
Deliver the hundred-kilo salt sacks to the weighbridge gate before nightfall.

choices.text: Replace runners on all five sledges. The convoy reaches the gate intact.
Abandon the three trailing sledges to save the lead draught animals. Half the salt is lost to the slush.

quests.briefing: A night tremor dropped forty tons of shale across the southern cut at Span 4. The supply haul from the switchback is completely halted. Pickaxe crews are needed to clear the roadbed before ice re-glazes over the rubble.

stages.text: Take heavy pry bars and survey the rockfall at Span 4.
Lever large granite boulders off the frozen ballast into the ravine.
Sledge the crushed shale flat to create a smooth runner track.
Signal the switchback lookouts that the southern corridor is open.

choices.text: Clear a double-wide lane for two-way sledge traffic.
Clear only a single-file footpath and push through immediately.

quests.briefing: Independent salt runners from Sector 4 are racing up the marked ice road to buy out the emergency fuel stores at Waystation A. If they corner the stock, prices will quadruple overnight.

stages.text: Harness the fast haulage team and push along the wind-scoured outer ice shelf.
Spot the rivals lanterns through the blowing spindrift at Kilometre 8.
Cut across the unlit salt pan shortcut to overtake their column.
Reach Waystation A first and lock in the municipal fuel contracts.

choices.text: Outrun them across the rough ice. The fuel is secured at civic rates.
Scatter caltrops on their track. Their lead sledge throws a runner.

quests.briefing: A lone courier carrying blood plasma and medical seals broke an axle three kilometres east of the river barge. The windchill is falling past minus thirty.

stages.text: Track the single sledge groove east from the river barge adit.
Find the overturned sledge half-buried in a drift.
Treat the courier for advanced frostbite and warm the insulated plasma flask.
Haul both courier and cargo back to the shelter dispensary.

choices.text: Haul the injured courier and the medical chest together.
Take only the blood plasma and leave the frozen runner.

quests.briefing: A gaunt survivor named Harek arrives at the weighbridge holding a soot-stained pre-war rent ledger, claiming hereditary rights to Room 12 in the sheltered lower tier.

stages.text: Cross-reference Hareks paper with Edor Vales master index.
Inspect the watermark under lamp oil to check for chemical erasure.
Interview the elders in Block B who remember the pre-war tenants.
Render a formal verdict on Hareks occupancy claim.

choices.text: Authenticate the ledger and assign Harek a bunk in Room 12.
Declare the document void due to water damage and reassign the bunk to working salters.

quests.briefing: Dozens of forged ration vouchers stamped with an obsolete purple seal have surfaced at the Caravanserai. Trace the source before the food reserves are drained.

stages.text: Confiscate the counterfeit slips from market traders.
Analyze the ink chemistry: lampblack mixed with elderberry dye.
Corner the engraver operating in the cellar behind the leather stalls.
Seize the carved copper stamp and decide the engravers fate.

choices.text: Hand the engraver over to the toll guards for trial.
Employ the engravers talent to forge trade passes into rival territory.

quests.briefing: Chief Machinist Aldis died in his sleep. His three apprentices and an estranged sister are fighting over his toolbox, coal rations, and winter bed allocation.

stages.text: Inventory Aldis tools, spare copper pipe, and stamped fuel scrip.
Listen to the apprentices arguments regarding shop continuity.
Hear the sisters claim regarding kinship support and family debt.
Partition the estate and record the final decree in the civic book.

choices.text: Give the machine tools to the workshop apprentices to keep the lathe running.
Award the tools and coal scrip to the sister to settle family debts.

quests.display_name: The Name Left on the Roll
quests.briefing: Scavenger Valeri has been overdue from the northern drifts for forty days. The Garrison conscription office wants to strike his name and seize his bunk for new recruits.

stages.text: Review Valeris expedition log and his last reported radio coordinates.
Present evidence of blizzard delays to the conscription clerk.
Pledge a personal deposit of dried rations to keep his claim active.
Witness the clerk stamp a twenty-day grace period on the roster.

choices.text: Pay the bond to keep Valeris name protected on the roster.
Allow the garrison to seize the bunk and take their ration reward.

quests.briefing: Crystalline calcium carbonate and gypsum scale have choked Boiler 3 at the desalination facility. If acid wash is not pumped within forty-eight hours, the steam jacket will rupture.

stages.text: Collect concentrated sulfuric acid carboys from the chemical store.
Flush the primary heat exchanger tubes under high pressure.
Scrape the caustic mineral slag out of the bottom blowdown trap.
Restart the draft fans and monitor boiler steam pressure.

choices.text: Run a full four-hour acid cycle. Boiler 3 efficiency restored to 95%.
Perform a hasty bypass. The boiler runs at half capacity with high blowout risk.

quests.briefing: The evaporation yard workers have laid down their shovels. Three men have salt-ulcers on their legs and the foreman has withheld tallow salve rations.

stages.text: Meet the striking salters at the edge of the shallow brine pans.
Inspect the chemical burns and salt dermatitis on their shins.
Confront Foreman Quist about the withheld medical supplies.
Broker a compromise on shift lengths and protective rubber waders.

choices.text: Force the foreman to release the medical tallow and shorten shifts.
Side with the foreman and threaten to cut meal rations if production halts.

quests.briefing: A slick of grey alkaline effluent has settled around Pump Station Nine. Two children drinking from the municipal outflow have fallen violently ill.

stages.text: Take water samples from Sluice 2 and test with litmus paper.
Trace the discharge upstream to an unmapped drainage culvert.
Discover an illicit battery-smelting operation dumping acid wash.
Shut down the illicit smelter and deploy activated charcoal filters.

choices.text: Dismantle the illegal battery furnace and cleanse the intake.
Impose an environmental levy on the smelter in exchange for lead ingots.

quests.briefing: Flotilla skiffs are siphoning fresh condensate directly from Lock Gate Four, depriving the downstream greenhouse terraces of irrigation water.

stages.text: Board the Flotilla flagship moored at the lock gate basin.
Inspect the greenhouse water levels and withered potato beds.
Chair a summit between Flotilla Captain Mallow and the Agronomist.
Sign a binding water distribution charter with fixed litre quotas.

choices.text: Direct eighty percent of freshwater to the food crops.
Grant the Flotilla their fuel-run water quota in exchange for fish rations.

quests.briefing: A hairline fracture in the shelter central heating duct has filled Block D with acrid carbon monoxide while outside temperatures plunge toward minus forty.

stages.text: Evacuate coughing residents from Block D into the crowded mess hall.
Locate the cracked cast-iron flue inside the crawlspace.
Braze the seam with bronze rod and fireproof asbestos paste.
Ventilate the toxic smoke through the emergency intake valves.

choices.text: Spend valuable bronze stock to seal the duct permanently.
Slap refractory clay over the crack and hope it holds through the winter.

quests.briefing: Desperate survivors from the overflow annex have smashed the outer padlock of the central grain vault after winter rations were cut by a third.

stages.text: Confront the angry mob holding torches outside the grain vault.
Inspect the damaged door and confirm no seed sacks were stolen.
Address their grievances regarding starvation rations and cold bunks.
Deliver a ruling on punishment and winter food allocation.

choices.text: Open an emergency grain sack and distribute warm porridge to defuse the riot.
Arrest the three crowbar wielders and enforce strict curfew.
